newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: New mayor appointed in Colombian capital.
newsitem.headline: New mayor appointed in Colombian capital.

text.p: President Ernesto Samper named a new mayor for the Colombian capital on Tuesday, three days after the city's former chief executive resigned to launch a bid for the presidency.
Samper named Paul Bromberg, a 45-year-old physicist, to fill the post which is often described as Colombia's second most important job.
Bromberg served under outgoing Mayor Antanas Mockus as head of Bogota's Cultural and Tourism Institute and he was one of three people on a short-list of candidates Mockus picked to succeed him.
Elections for a new mayor will be held in October and Bromberg will step down when Mockus' full term of office ends in December.

Recent polls indicate that Mockus, who is politically independent and a self-described "neo-anarchist," stands a good chance of making a strong showing in the presidential elections, which are scheduled for May 1998.
Under Colombian law, anybody seeking to run for the country's top job must resign from public office a full year before elections.
